title: Data and Integration
intro: The second-largest domain: how Pega models data (fields, data objects, relationships), keeps it correct (calculations, validation, defaults), and connects it to systems of record through data pages, refresh strategies, savable data pages and simulation. Expect scenario questions that hinge on one configuration word such as Refer vs Copy, Thread vs Node, or Lookup vs Data Transform.

objectives.objective: Explain the data model and its levels (conceptual, logical, physical)
summary: A data model is a picture of the data an application needs and how the pieces connect. It pays off in reuse, easier maintenance and the ability to adapt and scale; in practice the Lead System Architect reviews it before any data objects are created. Pega describes three levels of refinement. The conceptual model is drafted by the Business Architect with stakeholders and names entities, their attributes and the relationships between them; it is a living document whose purpose is to cut rework later. The logical model translates that picture into Pega terms: entities become data objects and attributes become fields. The physical model decides how data is stored and accessed, which is where integration settings live.

In App Studio the Integration Designer is the single place to see data objects, data pages, their dependencies and the external systems behind them, with an optional Integration Map diagram on top. The physical level is visible there. Each data object also has a visual Data Model diagram where fields can be added, changed or removed. All of this supports the center-out idea: the data access layer is insulated from business logic, so moving a system of record (for example from on-premises to the cloud) does not force changes to the logic or the views.
keyFacts: Conceptual model: owned by the Business Architect and stakeholders; entities, attributes, relationships; living document; reduces rework.
Logical model: Pega-specific refinement; entity maps to a data object, attribute maps to a field.
Physical model: storage and access details plus integration settings; surfaced in the Integration Designer.
The LSA verifies the data model before data objects are created.
Integration Designer (App Studio) = one place for data objects, data pages, dependencies and external systems; Integration Map is optional.
Data pages decouple integration from how the application uses data, so a source can change without changing views.
Center-out: data access layer insulated; changing the system of record does not require logic changes.
Benefits named for a data model: reuse, maintenance, adaptability/scalability.

rows: Business Architect + stakeholders; entities, attributes, relationships
How data is stored and accessed
Integration settings, data pages, external systems in Integration Designer

examTraps: Mapping entities to data objects is the logical level, not the conceptual one; the conceptual level is still tool-neutral.
Integration settings and storage choices belong to the physical model; do not pick 'logical' just because data objects are mentioned.
The conceptual model is not frozen after sign-off; it is described as a living document.

objectives.objective: Describe data types, data objects, relationships, data records and field types
summary: A field is a named, reusable element that holds one value per case (Dev Studio calls it a property). App Studio guesses the type from the name you type (default Text (single line); a name containing 'date' becomes Date only), so always check before submitting. Type choice matters: Integer drops leading zeros, so IDs and postal codes that are never used in arithmetic should be Text; money should be Currency (codes and separators) rather than Decimal; Date & time values are normalized to UTC/GMT; Email, Phone and URL render as action links and Email/URL include validation; Percentage shows .5 as 50%; Address adapts its fields to the selected country; User reference points at operators mapped to the app. Fancy types include Attachment and Location.

A data object is a template that groups related fields together with their views, rules and calculations, and can be reused across case types and even several times in one case (source and target account). Objects can inherit (Person-Customer) and can be sourced from a local Pega system of record, an external SOR, or nothing at all when the case captures the data. Best practice: use a standard object such as Address-Postal or Address-Email, extend one that partially fits (Person-Employee), and only then create a new one. A data object added from the workflow starts as a draft and must be made permanent on the Data objects and integrations page. A data record is one instance of a data object; locally it is a row in a database table shown on the Records tab. Changing records is a data change, while changing the fields is a process change. Records from an external source are not stored in Pega.

Relationships are containers that relate data without storing it themselves. Embedded data keeps user-entered data inside the case in a consistent format. Data reference reuses a data object that lives outside the case (local records or external SOR). Case reference pulls data from another case. Query is a read-only, parameterized lookup of external data. Each can be a single record or a list. Data reference supports Single, List and Many to Many modes.
keyFacts: Default inferred field type is Text (single line); names containing 'date' become Date only.
Integer strips leading zeros; use Text (single line) for IDs and zip codes without arithmetic.
Use Currency, not Decimal, for money; Date & time is stored normalized to UTC/GMT.
Email, Phone and URL show as action links; Email and URL include built-in validation.
Data object sourcing: local Pega SOR, external SOR, or none (entered in the case).
Reuse order: standard object (Address-Postal, Address-Email) -> extend a partial fit (Person-Employee) -> create new.
Draft data objects created from the workflow must be made permanent on the Data objects and integrations page.
Editing records = data change; adding/changing fields = process change.
Embedded list UI: Table or Field Group; Case reference UI: Autocomplete, Dropdown, Table; Data reference list UI: Table, Simple table, Combobox, Checkbox group.
Query fields need a list or lookup data page, use external parameters, and do not store the key.

Outside the case: local records or external SOR
Ordering customer; Product selected in a line item
Related policy case shown in a claim
External, read-only, parameterized via a data page

examTraps: Numeric-looking identifiers (badge numbers, zip codes) are a trap for Integer: leading zeros are lost.
Embedded data copies values into the case; for shared catalog-style data that lives elsewhere, pick Data reference.
Query is read-only and does not store the key, so it is wrong when the user's selection must be saved.
Draft data objects are not automatically permanent.

summary: App Studio lets a field be calculated instead of entered, in either a case type's or a data object's data model. There are three calculation kinds. Functions iterate over a list and return the Sum, Average, Maximum or Minimum of a field; they only produce Decimal, Currency or Integer results. Expressions combine fields with the dot operator, arithmetic (+ - * /), parentheses and AND/OR, and can concatenate text with quoted literals; they can return any simple type except Email, Phone and Picklist. Decision tables map conditions to a result.

Calculated fields form a calculation network: when an input changes, every dependent field recalculates automatically. Creating a custom decision table from App Studio is only available in Constellation applications; a decision table built in Dev Studio can be selected in App Studio only after it is marked as a relevant record. Decision tables evaluate rows top to bottom, return the first row whose conditions are all true, and use an 'otherwise' result as a guaranteed fallback.
keyFacts: Three calculation types in App Studio: Functions, Expressions, Decision tables.
Functions iterate a list: Sum of, Average of, Maximum of, Minimum of.
Function results limited to Decimal, Currency and Integer.
Expressions: dot operator, + - * /, parentheses, AND/OR, text concatenation with quotes.
Expressions can return any simple type except Email, Phone and Picklist.
Custom decision tables in App Studio: Constellation apps only.
Dev Studio decision tables must be marked relevant records to be used in App Studio.
The calculation network recalculates dependent fields automatically when inputs change.
Decision table: first matching row wins (top to bottom); 'otherwise' guarantees a result.

rows: Aggregate a list (sum, average, max, min)
Result must be Decimal, Currency or Integer
Not for Email, Phone, Picklist results
Condition combinations mapped to a result
Custom DT in App Studio only for Constellation; Dev Studio DT must be relevant

examTraps: Totaling a field across an embedded list is a Function (Sum of), not an Expression.
A Picklist result cannot come from an Expression even though Text can.
In a Traditional UI app, a missing App Studio option to build a decision table is expected behaviour, not a permissions problem.

objectives.objective: Apply validation rules and business logic to data
summary: Validation answers three questions: is the value the right type (handled by field type and control), is it one of the allowed values (lists/picklists), and does it make business sense (conditions). A calendar control guarantees a real date, but not that the date is in the past; that needs a business condition. In App Studio, a validation condition describes the invalid case and produces an error that blocks progress until fixed. The comparison can be against a constant or another field. Validations attach to a specific step instance, so the same field can carry different rules on different forms (a previous job's start date must be past; a new hire's start date must be future).

App Studio offers two trigger points: on form submit, where the user can correct the value immediately, and on stage entry, configured in the case type's Data model, which stops the case from entering the stage. With stage-entry validation the developer must give the user a way out, such as going back to a previous stage or closing the case. In Dev Studio, Validate rules (Process category) are attached to flow actions and extend App Studio validations; their Input tab can qualify when they run by input property, proposed work status, flow action or stage (stage-based equals App Studio stage-entry validation). Edit Validate rules use Java pattern checks on a property and are a security risk because of custom Java; set on the property's Advanced tab they run client-side as soon as the value changes, or they can be called from a Validate rule to run on submit. A library of validation functions covers checks like 'date within the past N weeks' or 'attachment of a category is present'.
keyFacts: Three validation needs: correct type, allowed values, business logic.
Calendar control ensures a valid date, not a past/future date.
App Studio validation conditions define the INVALID values.
Validations are tied to process step instances, so one field can have different validation per form.
Two App Studio trigger points: form submit and stage entry (stage entry configured in the case type Data model).
Stage-entry failures block entry; the designer must provide a recovery path.
Validate rules: Dev Studio, Process category, attached to flow actions; Input tab qualifies by property, proposed work status, flow action, stage.
Edit Validate rules: custom Java pattern checks (security risk); client-side immediately when set via 'Use Validate' on the property Advanced tab.
Validation function library: e.g., date within past N weeks, attachment of a category attached.

rows: Case tries to enter the stage
App Studio case type Data model (stage-based Validate rule)
Flow action submit, qualified on Input tab

examTraps: Required = Always forces a value but does not check business meaning.
Stage-entry validation is not 'immediate feedback on the form' — that is form-submit validation.
Edit Validate rules are not best practice for general logic: custom Java weakens security.

objectives.objective: Use data transforms and set default values (pyDefault, Data initialization, superclass)
modules: Application data manipulation in Dev Studio
summary: Data transforms copy and convert data (for example a text 'December 4, 2021' into a date), move it, calculate values, format it, and set defaults. In App Studio they run from a Run Data Transform automation step or as pre- or post-processing on a step; a classic case is post-processing on a shipping-information step that copies the shipping address to billing. In Dev Studio a flow connector can apply a data transform (Set properties > Apply Data Transform), and transforms can loop through lists, for example copying only child items with quantity above zero to the parent.

Defaults are best set on the Data initialization page of the case type Settings tab, which writes into the pyDefault data transform; use pyDefault directly for complex logic. pyDefault runs when the case is created and calls pySetFieldDefaults. pySetFieldDefaults runs when a view loads and is maintained by the system, so do not edit it. Both are generated the first time you create a view. To read operator details such as pyFirstName in a Dev Studio transform, the OperatorID page must be declared on the Pages & Classes tab. Functions such as @CurrentDateTime() and @addCalendar(...) help compute values.

The superclass feature chains same-named transforms through the class hierarchy. When 'Call superclass data transform' is checked, the runtime finds each parent transform up to the highest class and runs them top-down, so the most specific class runs last and its values win. It is turned on automatically when App Studio created default fields. Work- pyDefault sets status, urgency 10 and organization info; a case type pyDefault can override, for example urgency 40.
keyFacts: Data transform uses: copy/convert types, move data, calculate, format, set defaults.
App Studio entry points: Run Data Transform automation, step pre-/post-processing.
Dev Studio: apply a transform on a flow connector (Set properties > Apply Data Transform).
Best practice for simple defaults: Data initialization page (Settings tab) which updates pyDefault.
pyDefault runs at case creation and calls pySetFieldDefaults.
pySetFieldDefaults runs on view load, is system-maintained and should not be modified.
Both pyDefault and pySetFieldDefaults are created the first time a view is created.
OperatorID page must be on the Pages & Classes tab to reference pyFirstName/pyLastName.
Superclass chaining: parents run top-down, subclass values override; Work- pyDefault sets urgency 10.
For parent-child data, referencing avoids the synchronization issues of copying.
examTraps: Do not customize pySetFieldDefaults for complex logic; use pyDefault.
With superclass enabled the subclass runs last, so its value (e.g., urgency 40) wins over Work- (10).
A reference to OperatorID failing in a transform is usually a missing Pages & Classes entry, not a relevant-record issue.

objectives.objective: Configure sourced data: data pages, scope, sources, parameters, refresh strategies, refer vs copy, and populating UI controls
modules: Accessing sourced data in a Case
summary: Data pages (prefix D_) retrieve and cache data and keep integration details out of the process; they also support persistence and services. They load on demand when referenced: the system checks the cache, queries the source if the page is missing or stale, and returns the result. A data object with a system of record gets three default pages: a list (D_xxxList), a single-record lookup (D_xxx) and a savable page (D_xxxSavable). The definition sets the structure (Page or List, with list items in pxResults), the object type (class), the edit mode (Read-Only, Editable, or Savable with a save plan) and the scope: Thread (per case/transaction), Requestor (per user session) or Node (shared by all users).

Sources include Data Transform, Activity, Connector, Report definition, Database lookup, Robotic Automation, Robotic desktop Automation, Lookup and Aggregate sources (several sources run in listed order). With multiple conditional sources the first true condition wins and the last is the Otherwise. Parameters narrow the content (lookup key, report filter) using D_Name[p1:v1,p2:v2]; each distinct parameter combination is its own instance unless 'Limit to a single data page' is set on the Load Management tab. Parameters have a name, data type, required flag and In/Out direction.

Refresh strategies are optional but strongly recommended; the page reloads if any configured condition is met, and never more than once per interaction. 'Reload once per interaction' works only for Thread or Requestor scope and cannot be combined with other options. 'Do not reload when' treats the page as current while its When condition is true. 'Reload if older than' marks the page stale after an interval, and it reloads on the next access. A property can Refer to a data page (always current, no copy held by the case, a parameter change points it at a new instance) or Copy data from it (a point-in-time snapshot stored in the case, re-retrieved only when parameters change). For list controls such as dropdowns, only the selected value is copied to the case, and it can differ from the displayed value.
keyFacts: Default data pages for a data object with a SOR: D_xxxList, D_xxx (lookup), D_xxxSavable.
List structure stores rows in pxResults, e.g., D_X.pxResults(n).
Scope: Thread = per case/transaction; Requestor = per user session; Node = shared by all users.
Multiple sources: conditions evaluated in order, first true wins, last is Otherwise; Aggregate sources run in listed order.
Each parameter combination creates a separate instance unless 'Limit to a single data page' (Load Management tab).
Refresh: reload if ANY condition is met, never more than once per interaction.
'Reload once per interaction' is Thread/Requestor only and cannot be combined with other options.
'Reload if older than' does not reload in the background; it reloads on the next access after going stale.
Refer = always current, nothing stored in case; Copy = snapshot stored, refreshed only when parameters change.
List controls copy only the selected value; Constellation cascading dropdowns use two Picklist fields and a parameterized data page.

rows: One per case/transaction (stock price for this transaction)
One per user session (this customer's shipping addresses)
Shared by all users (vehicle makes and models)
When true, page is current (stocks after market close)
Stale after interval; reloads on next access
Always current; no copy in case
Copy data from a data page
Snapshot stored in case; re-fetch only when parameters change

examTraps: 'Reload once per interaction' on a Node-scoped page is invalid.
Refresh strategies are optional (though strongly recommended); a missing strategy is not a save error.
If the case must remember values as they were at a point in time, choose Copy, not Refer.
Parameterized pages create one instance per parameter set; this is expected, not a leak.

objectives.objective: Save data to a system of record (savable data pages, save plans, Save Data Page automation)
modules: Saving data to a system of record
summary: A savable data page writes a page or page list back to a system of record, inside Pega or external, in real time with transaction handling, so a failure rolls back both the case and the data save. The save plan lists save options, each with a When condition and an Otherwise: Database save (one page to one row, page structure only, transactional, mapped with a data transform), Database update, Database delete, Connector (REST only, not SOAP), Robotic automation (unattended RPA), Robotic desktop automation (RDA) and Activity (custom code; can call any connector including SOAP; not inherently transactional, so use sparingly).

The save is triggered by a Save Data Page automation step placed after the assignment, by post-processing on a flow action, or by the Save-DataPage method in an activity (which can choose the same or a separate transaction). In the Save Data Page step you either name the data page and its parameters explicitly or pick 'Use associated property' to take the page and parameters from an autopopulated property; one step per data source, and you can add an audit note. If a property is autopopulated from a savable data page, use Copy, not Refer, to avoid overwriting. To support both create and update, make the key parameter optional: when a key is supplied a Lookup source loads the existing record; when it is not, a Data Transform source initializes a new one. Best practice is to give savable pages used for creation an Index parameter (unless autopopulating by copy), which avoids a guardrail warning and allows multiple uses on one screen. Data objects also offer an Update Details action for changing only the needed information.
keyFacts: Savable data pages save in real time with transaction handling; failures roll back case and data together.
Database save: single page to single row; page structure only; transactional.
Connector save option supports REST only; SOAP requires the Activity option.
Activity save option is not inherently transactional; limit its use.
Triggers: Save Data Page step (after the assignment), flow action post-processing, Save-DataPage activity method.
Save Data Page step: explicit page + parameters, or 'Use associated property'; one step per source; optional audit note.
Autopopulated property backed by a savable page: use Copy, not Refer.
Update existing: key present -> Lookup source. Create new: no key -> Data Transform source. Key optional for both.
Best practice: Index parameter on savable pages that create records (avoids guardrail, multiple uses on a screen).

rows: One page -> one row; page structure only; transactional; data transform mapping
Custom; any connector incl. SOAP; not inherently transactional

examTraps: Connector save option does not support SOAP.
Database save does not handle page lists into multiple rows; it is one page to one row.
Using Refer with a savable page risks overwriting user edits; Copy also helps avoid stale page errors.
Multiple target systems mean multiple Save Data Page steps, not one step with several sources.

objectives.objective: Simulate data for development and testing
modules: Accessing sourced data in a Case
summary: When an external system is not available yet, has no data, or its API is still being built, a data page can use a simulated data source as a temporary stand-in. You need to know the expected request and response so the simulation matches reality. Simulation lets the UI team keep working and is useful for unit testing because you control the response. It must be replaced by the real source before production.

For local data, Autopilot can fill a data object with realistic sample records from the Records tab ('Generate sample records with Autopilot', choosing how many); values match the field types (an Email field gets email-shaped values). This is a good substitute for a system of record that is not integrated yet during testing.
keyFacts: Simulate when the external system is unavailable, has no data, or the API is still in development.
Expected request and response structures must be known.
Simulation dictates responses, which helps unit testing; the UI team is not blocked.
Simulated data pages are temporary: configure the real source before production.
Autopilot generates sample records on a data object's Records tab; you choose the count and values match field types.
examTraps: Simulation is never acceptable as the production source, even if responses look correct.
Autopilot sample records do not sync to the external system later; they are test data only.

questions.stem: Stakeholder workshops produced a list of entities (Policy, Claimant, Vehicle) and their attributes. The LSA now maps each entity to a data object and each attribute to a field. Which data model level is the LSA producing?
options: Conceptual data model
Logical data model
Physical data model
Integration Map
questions.explanation: Mapping entities to data objects and attributes to fields is the logical level, the Pega-specific refinement. The conceptual model is the tool-neutral stakeholder view that already exists here. The physical model covers storage, access and integration settings, which have not been decided yet. The Integration Map is an optional diagram in the Integration Designer, not a level of the data model.

questions.stem: An insurer moves its policy system of record from an on-premises database to a cloud REST API. The case types read policy data through data pages. Which two statements about this change are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Views that display policy data do not need to change
The change belongs to the physical level of the data model
The conceptual model must be signed off again before the change
Case business logic must be rewritten to call the new API
questions.explanation: Data pages separate integration from how the application uses data, and the center-out approach insulates the data access layer, so views and logic stay as they are. Storage and access decisions such as the source system are physical-level concerns. The conceptual model describes entities and relationships, which have not changed, and it is a living document anyway, not something that blocks integration work. Rewriting business logic is exactly what the insulated data access layer avoids.

questions.stem: An onboarding case captures a six-digit Badge number that can start with 0 and a Signing bonus in the employee's local currency. Which two field type choices are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Badge number as Text (single line)
Signing bonus as Currency
Signing bonus as Decimal, which supports currency codes
Badge number as Integer, because it holds only digits
questions.explanation: Integer strips leading zeros, so an identifier that is never used in arithmetic belongs in Text (single line). Money belongs in Currency, which handles currency codes and separators. Decimal is a real numeric type but it is the currency type, not Decimal, that supports codes and separators. Integer would turn a badge such as 012345 into 12345.

questions.stem: In an Order case, each order line holds a Quantity entered by the user and one Product chosen from a catalog stored as local Pega records. How should the Ordered items field be modeled?
options: Embedded data list whose items include a Product data reference
Data reference list pointing to the Product data object
Query field that returns the product catalog
Case reference list pointing to Product cases
questions.explanation: Quantity is user-entered data that lives in the case, so the line items are an embedded data list, and each line reuses the shared catalog through a single Product data reference. A data reference list alone has nowhere to store the per-line Quantity. A Query field is read-only and does not store the key, so the chosen product would not be saved. Products are data records, not cases, so a case reference does not fit.

questions.stem: Claim CL-88 shows details from its related Policy case. It also shows a read-only list of repair shops from an external API, filtered by postal code; the user's view of the list is not saved. Which two relationship field types fit? (Choose Two)
options: Case reference for the related Policy
Query for the repair shop list
Embedded data for the repair shop list
Data reference for the related Policy, since it lives outside the claim
questions.explanation: Data that comes from another case uses a Case reference. A read-only, parameterized lookup of external data that is not stored by key is a Query. Embedded data is for user-entered data stored inside the case, which the shop list is not. Data reference does reuse data from outside the case, but it points at data objects, not at another case, so the qualifier makes it wrong.

questions.stem: On the same day, an analyst adds 40 rows on the Records tab of the Product data object, and a developer adds a Warranty period field to the same data object. Which statement about these changes is correct?
options: The new rows are a data change; the new field is a process change
Both are data changes because only a data object was touched
Both are process changes because the data model was edited
The new rows are a process change; the new field is a data change
questions.explanation: Editing records changes data only, while adding or changing fields changes the application's structure and counts as a process change. Treating both as one kind ignores that distinction, whether because only a data object was touched or because the data model was edited. Swapping the two labels gets both of them wrong.

questions.stem: While configuring a step in a case lifecycle, a developer adds a new Vendor data object from the workflow. What must happen for Vendor to become a permanent part of the application?
options: Make it permanent on the Data objects and integrations page
Mark it as a relevant record in Dev Studio
Add it to the case type's Data initialization page
Nothing; objects added from the workflow are permanent already
questions.explanation: A data object added from the workflow starts as a draft and must be made permanent on the Data objects and integrations page. Relevant records control what App Studio users can pick from Dev Studio rules, not draft status. The Data initialization page sets default values through pyDefault. Draft objects are not automatically permanent.

questions.stem: An HR application needs an employee's postal address and an Employee data object. The standard Person data object covers most employee fields but not all of them. Which two choices follow data object best practice? (Choose Two)
options: Reuse the standard Address-Postal object for the address
Extend Person as Person-Employee
Create a new Employee Address object to keep HR data separate
Create a standalone Employee object because Person fits only partly
questions.explanation: The recommended order is to use a standard object first, extend one that partially fits, and create a new object only as a last resort. Address-Postal is a standard object for this need, and Person-Employee extends a partial fit. A separate Employee Address object duplicates a standard one. A partial fit is exactly the case for extending, not for building a standalone object.

questions.stem: An Expense report case has an embedded list of Expense lines, each with an Amount of type Currency. The case needs a Total that updates as lines change. Which configuration is correct?
options: A Function calculation using Sum of on Amount
An Expression that adds each line's Amount with +
A Decision table that returns the total
A default set on the Data initialization page
questions.explanation: Functions iterate over a list and return Sum, Average, Maximum or Minimum, and the calculation network recalculates the total when a line changes. An Expression combines individual fields with operators; it does not iterate a list of unknown length. A Decision table maps conditions to a result, not an aggregate. The Data initialization page sets a value once at case creation, so it would not track changes.

questions.stem: A developer is adding calculated fields in App Studio. Which two configurations are valid? (Choose Two)
options: An Expression returning Text that joins First and Last name with " "
A Function returning the Maximum of a Currency field across a list
An Expression returning a Picklist value based on Amount
A Function returning the Average of a list into a Text field
questions.explanation: Expressions can return any simple type except Email, Phone and Picklist, and they can concatenate text with quoted literals, so a Text full name is valid. Functions can return Maximum of a list into Currency, one of the three allowed result types. A Picklist result is one of the exclusions for Expressions. Average of is a real Function, but Function results are limited to Decimal, Currency and Integer, so a Text target is invalid.

questions.stem: In a Traditional UI application, a citizen developer cannot find the option to create a custom decision table for a calculated field. A table that an SA built in Dev Studio for this purpose is also missing from the list. Which statement explains both problems?
options: Custom tables need Constellation, and the Dev Studio table is not a relevant record
The citizen developer's access role lacks permission to create decision tables
Calculated fields can use When rules but not decision tables
The Dev Studio table must first be copied into the Data- class
questions.explanation: Creating a custom decision table from App Studio is available only in Constellation applications, and a Dev Studio decision table appears in App Studio only after it is marked as a relevant record. This is expected behavior, not a permissions gap. Decision tables are one of the three App Studio calculation types. Class placement is not the condition for visibility; relevant-record status is.

questions.stem: The Start date field appears on the Prior employment step, where it must be in the past, and on the New hire step, where it must be in the future. Both steps use a calendar control. Which approach is correct?
options: Add a separate validation to each step
Rely on the calendar control to reject the wrong dates
Add one validation to the field so it applies everywhere
Create two Start date fields, since a field holds one validation
questions.explanation: Validations are tied to a specific step instance, so the same field can carry a past-date rule on one form and a future-date rule on another. A calendar control only guarantees a real date, not one in the past or future. A single rule cannot express two opposite conditions. Duplicating the field is unnecessary because one field can carry different validations on different forms.

questions.stem: Loan case LN-204 must not enter the Underwriting stage unless Collateral value is at least the Loan amount. Which two statements about configuring this in App Studio are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Configure it as a stage-entry validation in the case type Data model
Provide a way out, such as returning to a previous stage
The user sees the error immediately on the form that captured the value
The condition describes the valid values that permit entry
questions.explanation: Stage-entry validation is configured in the case type's Data model and stops the case from entering the stage, so the designer must give the user a recovery path such as going back a stage or closing the case. Immediate feedback on the form is form-submit validation, the other trigger point. App Studio validation conditions describe the invalid values that raise an error, not the valid ones.

questions.stem: In Dev Studio, a Validate rule must run when the proposed work status is Pending-Qualification but not when it is Approved. Where is this configured?
options: On the Validate rule's Input tab
On the property's Advanced tab with Use Validate
In an Edit Validate rule's Java pattern
On the case type's Data initialization page
questions.explanation: The Input tab of a Validate rule qualifies when it runs by input property, proposed work status, flow action or stage. The Advanced tab's Use Validate setting attaches an Edit Validate rule to a property and runs client-side, with no status condition. An Edit Validate rule checks a value's pattern, not case status. The Data initialization page sets defaults, not validation conditions.

questions.stem: An SA considers Edit Validate rules to check the format of a Policy number. Which two statements are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Set through the property's Advanced tab, it runs client-side on value change
It is a security risk because it uses custom Java
Called from a Validate rule, it still runs client-side on value change
It is the preferred place for general business logic
questions.explanation: An Edit Validate rule set with Use Validate on the property's Advanced tab runs client-side as soon as the value changes, and its custom Java pattern checks are a security risk. When a Validate rule calls it, it runs on submit, not on value change, so that qualifier is wrong. Because of the custom Java, Edit Validate is not best practice for general logic.

questions.stem: Work- pyDefault sets urgency 10. The Claim case type's pyDefault sets urgency 40 and has Call superclass data transform checked. What is the urgency of a new claim, and why?
options: 40, because parent transforms run first and the subclass runs last
10, because Work- runs last and overrides the subclass
10, because superclass values take priority over subclasses
40, because Work- is skipped when the subclass has its own transform
questions.explanation: With the superclass option checked, the runtime finds each same-named parent transform and runs them top-down, so the most specific class runs last and its value wins. Work- runs first, not last, so it cannot override the subclass. Superclass values do not take priority; they are the starting point. Work- is not skipped; it still sets status, urgency and organization details before the subclass overrides urgency.

questions.stem: A Permit case needs Priority defaulted to Normal and a Review date computed with @addCalendar from several conditions. Which two choices follow best practice? (Choose Two)
options: Set Priority on the Data initialization page of the Settings tab
Put the Review date logic in pyDefault
Put the Review date logic in pySetFieldDefaults, which runs on view load
Set Priority by editing pySetFieldDefaults directly
questions.explanation: Simple defaults belong on the Data initialization page, which writes into pyDefault, and complex logic goes in pyDefault directly. pySetFieldDefaults does run when a view loads, but it is system-maintained and should not be modified, so neither the Review date logic nor the Priority default belongs there.

questions.stem: A Dev Studio data transform sets Requester name from pyFirstName on the OperatorID page, but the value never resolves. Which change most likely fixes it?
options: Declare OperatorID on the Pages & Classes tab
Mark the data transform as a relevant record
Check Call superclass data transform
Move the step into pySetFieldDefaults
questions.explanation: To reference operator details such as pyFirstName in a Dev Studio transform, the OperatorID page must be declared on the Pages & Classes tab. Relevant-record status affects visibility in App Studio, not runtime page references. The superclass option chains parent transforms and does nothing for page declarations. pySetFieldDefaults is system-maintained and should not be edited.

questions.stem: On the Shipping information step, the user enters a shipping address. The billing address must match it once the user submits the step. Which configuration is correct?
options: A data transform as post-processing on the Shipping information step
A data transform as pre-processing on the Shipping information step
A form-submit validation on the Shipping information step
An Expression calculation on the billing address fields
questions.explanation: Post-processing runs after the user submits, when the shipping address exists, so a data transform there can copy it to billing. Pre-processing runs before the form is shown, when there is nothing to copy yet. A validation checks values and raises errors; it does not copy data. A calculated Expression cannot return an Address, which is not a simple type, and copying is the job of a data transform.

questions.stem: A list of vehicle makes and models is used by every user of the application and changes only every 30 to 60 days. Which data page configuration fits best?
options: Node scope with Reload if older than
Node scope with Reload once per interaction
Thread scope with Reload if older than
Requestor scope with Reload once per interaction
questions.explanation: Data shared by all users belongs in Node scope, and a long Reload if older than interval balances performance with occasional changes. Reload once per interaction is not valid for Node scope. Thread scope would load a copy per case or transaction, wasting the shared nature of the data. Requestor scope with a reload on every interaction loads a per-user copy far more often than data that changes monthly needs.

questions.stem: D_StockQuote supplies prices to a trading case. Which two statements about its refresh strategy are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Do not reload when can keep the page current after market close
The page reloads when any one configured condition is met
Reload once per interaction can be combined with Reload if older than
The data page cannot be saved without a refresh strategy
questions.explanation: Do not reload when treats the page as current while its When condition is true, which suits prices after market close, and the page reloads if any configured condition is met. Reload once per interaction is a real option but it cannot be combined with other options. Refresh strategies are optional, though strongly recommended, so a page without one can still be saved.

questions.stem: D_ExchangeRates uses Reload if older than 10 minutes. It is first accessed at 12:00 and next accessed at 13:00. Which statement is correct?
options: It becomes stale at 12:10 and reloads when accessed at 13:00
It reloads automatically in the background at 12:10
It reloads every 10 minutes from 12:10 onwards
It reloads only when the requestor session ends
questions.explanation: Reload if older than marks the page stale after the interval and reloads it on the next access, here 13:00. It does not reload in the background at 12:10 or on a repeating timer. Session end has nothing to do with this strategy.

questions.stem: Credit case CR-310 must keep the applicant's credit score as it was at application time, even if the bureau later updates it. How should the Credit score property be populated?
options: Copy data from a data page
Refer to a data page
Refer to a data page with Reload once per interaction
Refer to a Node-scoped data page
questions.explanation: Copy stores a point-in-time snapshot in the case that is re-retrieved only if the parameters change. Refer keeps no copy in the case and always reflects the current data page, so the score would change when the bureau updates it. Adding a refresh strategy or a wider scope to a Refer makes the value even more current, not frozen.

questions.stem: Property .Customer refers to D_Customer[CustomerID:.CustID]. Which two statements are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Changing .CustID points .Customer to a different data page instance
The case holds no copy of the customer data
The case keeps a snapshot refreshed only when .CustID changes
A new .CustID overwrites the one existing D_Customer instance
questions.explanation: With Refer, the case stores no copy, and a parameter change points the property at a new data page instance. A stored snapshot that refreshes only on parameter change describes Copy, not Refer. Each distinct parameter value creates its own instance unless Limit to a single data page is set, so values are not overwritten in one instance by default.

questions.stem: D_Product[ProductID] now holds instances for 500 different product IDs in one session. The team wants only one instance kept at a time. Which change achieves this?
options: Select Limit to a single data page on the Load Management tab
Change the scope from Thread to Node
Add Reload once per interaction as the refresh strategy
Change the structure from Page to List
questions.explanation: Each parameter combination creates its own instance unless Limit to a single data page is selected on the Load Management tab. Node scope shares instances across users but still keeps one per parameter value. A refresh strategy controls when a page reloads, not how many instances exist. Changing to a List structure changes the shape of the result, not the per-parameter instances.

questions.stem: D_Customer has three conditional sources in this order: a REST connector when Region is EU, a report definition when Region is US, and a data transform as Otherwise. Which two statements are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Source conditions are evaluated in the listed order
The first source whose condition is true is used
Every source whose condition is true runs in sequence
The Otherwise source can be placed anywhere in the list
questions.explanation: With multiple conditional sources, conditions are checked in order and the first true one supplies the data. Running several sources in listed order is the Aggregate sources option, not conditional sources. The Otherwise source is always the last one, so it cannot be placed anywhere.

questions.stem: A flight seating data page must show the latest seat availability on every user interaction. Which configuration is valid?
options: Thread scope with Reload once per interaction
Node scope with Reload once per interaction
Thread scope with Reload once per interaction and Reload if older than
Node scope with Do not reload when
questions.explanation: Reload once per interaction refreshes on each interaction and is valid for Thread or Requestor scope. It is not allowed in Node scope. It cannot be combined with other options such as Reload if older than. Do not reload when keeps the page unchanged while its condition is true, which does not guarantee fresh data on each interaction.

questions.stem: A Country dropdown is sourced from a list data page. Users see country names, but the case must store the two-letter country code. Which statement is correct?
options: Only the selected value is copied, and it can differ from the displayed text
The full country list is copied into the case when a value is chosen
The displayed name is stored, so a data transform must convert it
The dropdown needs a savable data page to store the code
questions.explanation: List controls copy only the selected value into the case, and that value can be different from what is displayed, such as a code instead of a name. The list itself stays on the data page. No conversion transform is needed because the stored value can be configured directly. Savable data pages write data back to a system of record; they are not required to store a selection.

questions.stem: A Customer data object is connected to an external system of record. Which two data pages does Pega create for it by default? (Choose Two)
options: D_CustomerList, a list data page
D_CustomerSavable, a savable data page
D_CustomerNode, a Node-scoped cache page
Declare_Customer, a declarative lookup page
questions.explanation: A data object with a system of record gets three default pages: D_CustomerList, the lookup D_Customer and D_CustomerSavable. There is no default page named for its scope. Declare_ was the prefix before version 7.1; current data pages use D_.

questions.stem: A Vendor case must save new vendors to an external SOAP service through a savable data page. Which save option should be used?
options: Activity
Connector
Database save
Robotic desktop automation
questions.explanation: The Activity save option can call any connector, including SOAP. The Connector save option supports REST only. Database save writes a page to a row in a database table, not to a service. Robotic desktop automation drives desktop applications, not a SOAP service.

questions.stem: Case DP-55 collects a list of Dependents and writes them to a local table through a savable data page. Which two statements are correct? (Choose Two)
options: A Database save maps one page to one row
If the save fails, the case and the data save roll back together
A Database save writes a page list as multiple rows in one save
The Activity save option is transactional by default
questions.explanation: Database save handles a single page to a single row with the page structure only, and savable data pages use transaction handling so a failure rolls back both the case and the data. Database save does not write a page list into multiple rows in one save. The Activity option is not inherently transactional, which is why its use should be limited.

questions.stem: One savable data page, D_SupplierSavable, must both create new suppliers and update existing ones. How should it be configured?
options: Optional key; Lookup source when a key is given, Data Transform source when not
Required key; Data Transform source when a key is given, Lookup source when not
Two separate savable data pages, one for create and one for update
Optional key; Lookup source when no key is given
questions.explanation: Making the key optional lets one page do both: with a key, a Lookup source loads the existing record to update; without one, a Data Transform source initializes a new record. A required key prevents creation, and the sources are swapped in that option. Two pages are unnecessary. A Lookup with no key has no record to load.

questions.stem: After an assignment, case CU-19 must update a customer record in a Pega table and also send it to an external REST billing system. Which two statements about the Save Data Page steps are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Add one Save Data Page step for each data source
Place the steps after the assignment that collects the data
Use one step that lists both sources and saves them in order
Place the steps before the assignment so data saves as entered
questions.explanation: A Save Data Page step handles one data source, so two targets need two steps, and the steps go after the assignment that gathers the data. A single step cannot list both sources. Placing the steps before the assignment would save before the user has entered anything.

questions.stem: Property .Customer is autopopulated from D_CustomerSavable by Refer. Users edit the address on a form, but their edits are overwritten before the save. Which change fixes this?
options: Change .Customer to Copy data from the data page
Change the data page scope from Thread to Node
Add Reload once per interaction to the data page
Move the save into flow action pre-processing
questions.explanation: With a savable data page, the autopopulated property should use Copy, not Refer: Refer always shows the data page, so a reload can overwrite user edits, and Copy also helps avoid stale page errors. Node scope would share one page across all users, which makes the problem worse. Reloading every interaction overwrites edits more often. Saves are triggered by a step or post-processing; pre-processing runs before the user even edits.

questions.stem: A developer needs a savable data page save to run in a transaction separate from the case. Which trigger allows this choice?
options: The Save-DataPage method in an activity
A Save Data Page automation step with an audit note
Post-processing on the flow action
Use associated property in the Save Data Page step
questions.explanation: When the Save-DataPage method is called from an activity, the activity can choose the same transaction or a separate one. The Save Data Page step can add an audit note, flow action post-processing is another valid trigger, and Use associated property takes the page and parameters from an autopopulated property, but none of them offers a separate-transaction choice.

questions.stem: A form lets a user add two new Contact records on one screen, both through D_ContactSavable. The property is not autopopulated by Copy, and a guardrail warning appears. Which change follows best practice?
options: Add an Index parameter to the savable data page
Select Limit to a single data page on the Load Management tab
Change the save option from Database save to Activity
Change the scope to Node so both forms share one page
questions.explanation: Best practice is to give a savable data page that creates records an Index parameter, unless it is autopopulated by Copy. This avoids the guardrail warning and allows multiple uses on one screen. Limiting to a single data page would make both contacts share one instance. The save option does not affect the guardrail. Node scope would share one page with every user.

questions.stem: The billing REST API is still being built. The UI team needs to keep working, and testers want predictable responses for unit tests. Which two statements about a simulated data source are correct? (Choose Two)
options: The expected request and response structures must be known
It lets testers dictate the response the data page returns
It may stay as the production source if responses match
It needs the external system online to record responses
questions.explanation: A simulation must match the expected request and response, and because it dictates the response it is useful for unit testing while the UI team keeps moving. A simulation is always temporary and must be replaced by the real source before production, however good the responses look. It exists precisely because the external system is unavailable, so it does not need that system online.

questions.stem: A local Supplier data object has no records yet. Testers need about 50 realistic suppliers before the system of record is integrated. Which approach fits?
options: Generate sample records with Autopilot on the Records tab
Configure a simulated source on D_SupplierSavable
Import sample suppliers through a Blueprint into a Branch
Add a Data Transform source on D_SupplierList that builds 50 pages
questions.explanation: Autopilot can generate a chosen number of sample records on a data object's Records tab, with values that match each field type, and it is a good stand-in for an unintegrated system of record during testing. Simulation applies to a data page source for an external system, and a savable page writes data rather than supplying it. Blueprint builds the application design, not test records. A hand-built transform source is extra code that does not create real records.
